assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators opened a new class of electronic phases defined by topology and protected edge transport, with lasting influence across condensed matter, materials science and device concepts. The idea is original and the experimental realization is clear.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the decisive theory (quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 classification); Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells. This maps naturally onto a two-theory, one-experiment configuration. Other contributors (e.g. Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang for the HgTe proposal) are not in the supplied credit list, so the fairness of the allocation is not fully settled.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: confirmed in HgTe and many later materials, three-dimensional generalizations and a large independent literature, and recognition is arguably overdue. Timing is strong.
uncertainties: Credit for the HgTe proposal and the 3D generalizations lies partly outside the supplied names.
I rely on my own knowledge of the history and have not independently verified priority details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proposals and experiments for quantum computation and simulation with trapped ions and neutral atoms form a foundation of quantum information science; the Cirac-Zoller gate and the later digital and analogue quantum simulation programmes have had very broad impact on how controlled quantum systems are engineered.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are the central theorists, and Blatt represents the decisive ion-trap experimental realization of gates, entanglement and algorithms. Bloch's optical-lattice work is better treated under the separate Hubbard simulation entry, and the candidate is compound, so the three-person limit forces a difficult split between ions and neutral atoms and between theory and experiment.
assessment.maturity: Mature in trapped ions, with independent confirmation by many groups and commercial platforms. Neutral-atom simulation is also well established. The 2012 prize already honoured ion control by Wineland, so the incremental novelty must be argued carefully.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize for control of single quantum systems.
Compound discovery whose ion and neutral-atom parts may need different recognition.
Whether Wineland-adjacent experimentalists beyond the credited names deserve credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, with magic-wavelength trapping, delivers fractional uncertainties at the 10^-18 level and underpins redefinition of the second, tests of fundamental constants and relativistic geodesy. It is a clear, specific invention with large metrological impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice clock concept and first realized it; Ye drove the dramatic precision improvements and many-body clock work. The two-person configuration is clean, though Hall and Hansch were already honoured in 2005 and others (e.g. Lemke, Ludlow, Ye's collaborators, and the Paris, Boulder NIST groups) contributed to the demonstrations.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple independent laboratories operate lattice clocks and the CIPM is moving toward a redefinition of the second. Timing is good.
uncertainties: Share of credit relative to the ion-clock and frequency-comb communities.
Whether a prize on precision timekeeping would be viewed as a continuation of 2005.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at magic angles and the discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene created the field of moire quantum matter, an exceptionally productive and original platform for correlated and topological physics.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the decisive theoretical prediction of the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the experimental discovery of correlated states and superconductivity. Pablo Jarillo-Herrero is a clear experimental lead, but others (Cao, Fatemi, Dean, Young, Yankowitz, Morell and colleagues) contributed major parts and the credited trio leaves some allocation questions.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly maturing with strong independent replication, although the field is young and the microscopic origin of superconductivity remains debated. Recognition is probably timely rather than late.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism and many phases are not settled.
Credit for the early demonstration among many co-authors is contested in outline.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED established the architecture of strong light-matter coupling with superconducting qubits and microwave resonators, enabling dispersive readout, gates and error-correction experiments; it is a scientifically central and original development for quantum technology.
assessment.attribution: Blais and collaborators proposed the circuit analogue of cavity QED, while Wallraff and Schoelkopf demonstrated strong coupling in the lab; this is a natural theory/experiment pairing. Because the field involves close colleagues in my own research area, I flag a conflict of interest and a risk of bias and I rank it with that caution in mind.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed worldwide, but the 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in a circuit just honoured the superconducting-circuit line, so a prompt second award in the same area may be premature.
uncertainties: Declared proximity of my own field (Chalmers and WACQT) to this topic.
Proximity of the recently awarded superconducting-circuit work and overlap in the underlying physics.
Distinction between the invention of the architecture and the broader quantum computing engineering effort.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum cryptography, from BB84 to the entanglement-based Ekert protocol, turned quantum mechanics into a practical resource for secure communication and is one of the founding ideas of quantum information science.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard authored BB84, and Ekert independently proposed the entanglement-based E91 scheme, so the three names form a natural allocation. Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is an unresolved priority issue and is outside the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Conceptually mature and demonstrated in many experiments including satellite links, though the experimental and technological chain is not by one lab. The 2022 prize honoured entanglement tests and so partly overlaps in subject.
uncertainties: Wiesner's earlier conjugate coding and its attribution.
Whether the prize should reward a theoretical protocol rather than a demonstrated discovery of nature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rydberg blockade underlies programmable neutral-atom arrays used for quantum simulation and fast, high-fidelity quantum gates, an important and rapidly developing route to scalable quantum processors and a strong test of many-body physics.
assessment.attribution: Saffman contributed to the blockade gate proposals and demonstrations, Browaeys to the early blockade and array experiments, and Lukin to the large-scale programmable arrays and the original blockade idea along with Jaksch and Zoller (not credited here). The origin of the blockade proposal lies partly outside the supplied names, so the credit is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Fast-moving and increasingly confirmed by independent groups, but fault-tolerant performance is still being established; a prize may be somewhat premature compared with the stable platforms above.
uncertainties: Original blockade proposal by Jaksch, Cirac, Zoller and others is not in the credited names.
Eventual performance for error-corrected computing is not demonstrated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Conformal field theory gave exact descriptions of two-dimensional critical phenomena, string theory and quantum field theory; the work is deep, original and has lasting influence across statistical physics, condensed matter and high-energy theory.
assessment.attribution: Polyakov, with Belavin and Zamolodchikov, wrote the foundational BPZ construction; Cardy applied the theory to critical phenomena and finite-size scaling. The BPZ credit also includes Belavin, who is outside the supplied names, so the allocation leaves a significant gap.
assessment.maturity: Mature and universally accepted with extensive agreement with experiments and numerics, but the central results are decades old and the connection to a single decisive experimental discovery is indirect, which is a mixed fit with the prize's traditions.
uncertainties: Omission of Belavin from the credited names.
Whether a theory-only prize in this area would meet the experimental and discovery-based tradition.
